title.narrative: USAID/Uganda Maternal Child Health and Nutrition (MCHN) Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): MCHN will use FY 2022 MCH, FP, and Nutrition funds to support integrated, multi-sectoral maternal, newborn, and child health (MCH) and nutrition interventions cutting across the portfolio. MCHN will strengthen the Government of Uganda's performance in implementing strategies to improve MCH; water, sanitation, and hygiene; and nutrition outcomes. MCHN will contribute to health system strengthening to ensure services are accessible and affordable for all. It will focus specifically on governance and leadership, human resources for health, and data use at the national level. The key outcomes expected include: 1) improved rollout and uptake of priority MCH and nutrition strategies; 2) strengthened quality of MCH and nutrition services; 3) increased use of data to improve service delivery; 4) strengthened cooperation and coordination; and 5) good governance and leadership at national and regional levels to drive improved MCH and nutrition outcomes.MCHN will strengthen the integration and scale-up of immediate postpartum family planning during the postnatal period. It will strengthen the scale-up of key behavior change related to WASH and increased access to safe sanitation services within the health facilities. It will continue to ensure that the support provided is responsive to programming within the COVID context. It will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; 4) improve access and utilization of micronutrients; 5) improve access and utilization of vitamin A; and 6) improve WASH related outcomes at the household and facility level in implementation districts. By strengthening resilient health systems at national and sub-national level, the activity will respond to climate related service delivery disruptions..
